title: Iceland Referendum Rejects Reopening EU Accession Talks
detail: Icelanders voted 52.8% to 47.2% against reopening EU membership negotiations, which had been suspended since 2013, in a referendum held under the shadow of US President Trump's threats regarding Greenland. Turnout reached 82.5% of eligible voters. Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir, who had framed the vote as a 'now or never' moment and cast EU membership as a shield against trade wars and Arctic rivalry, pledged the issue would not return to the political agenda during her mandate (through 2028). Opponents argued Iceland's fishing waters — marine products made up nearly 47% of exports in the year to July 2026 — were too important to risk under the EU's Common Fisheries Policy. An EU diplomat told Reuters the result was 'a clear setback for Brussels'; Iceland will instead focus on deepening ties via the European Economic Area agreement it shares with Norway and Liechtenstein.
